capabilities.name: React, Vite, and TypeScript
capabilities.behavior: Builds a strict TypeScript React application with routed marketplace, sale, and inspector pages.
capabilities.limits: Pinned Node, package-manager, local build, and test gates must be rerun after material source changes.

capabilities.name: Frontend architecture
capabilities.behavior: Separates feature use cases, long-lived capabilities, and SDK adapters and checks dependency direction from both import syntax and resolved package ownership.
capabilities.limits: The checker covers parsed source imports; it is not a runtime isolation mechanism.

capabilities.name: Wallet connectivity
capabilities.behavior: Connects an injected EIP-1193 wallet or an explicitly enabled loopback demo connector and tracks connection and account lifecycle.
capabilities.limits: Missing-provider and connector-selection component tests passed. Browser settlement uses the loopback demo connector; fault injection uses a controlled provider. Manual MetaMask smoke testing is not recorded.

capabilities.name: Network validation and switching
capabilities.behavior: Checks local chain identity and surfaces wrong-network or rejected switch outcomes.
capabilities.limits: Only local chain ID 31337 is in scope.

capabilities.name: Smart-contract interaction
capabilities.behavior: Uses generated ABIs, simulates writes, and keeps approval separate from listing. Binds a seller-selected reserved buyer before funding.
capabilities.limits: No public-chain deployment or external wallet-provider compatibility claim.

capabilities.name: Transaction lifecycle
capabilities.behavior: Durably records immutable intent before wallet submission, rechecks full live deployment identity, observes canonical receipt outcomes for every supported action, keeps successful and reverted local receipts under non-final observation, preserves funding-specific projection proof, serializes same-profile browser writes, assigns operation-scoped cross-tab observation ownership, and preserves tab-local evidence when durable storage reads are unavailable. Assigns cross-tab submission ownership to one in-flight immutable intent before any await and exposes matching per-action pending state. Volatile transaction evidence can rebase only over a matching hashless durable revision. Candidate inspection validates the saved descriptor against configured contracts, the actual RPC chain, and the on-chain deployment getter before transaction lookup. Known-hash verification continues in the volatile overlay when a durable update fails. Immediately before wallet submission, the gateway proves the immutable deployment identity through both the public RPC and wallet provider. Models receipt inclusion and chain finality as separate evidence.
capabilities.limits: Non-durable known-hash tracking survives client-side route changes and storage read denial only in the current tab; reload or tab close loses it. Local non-final observation is not a public-network finality claim. Cross-tab observation and submission ownership require Web Locks; their fallbacks coordinate one JavaScript realm only. Cross-device journal coordination and manual MetaMask response-loss testing are not claimed.

capabilities.name: Frontend state and API integration
capabilities.behavior: Keeps query cache, wallet state, form state, transaction journal, and projection provenance in separate owners. Deployment-keyed queries pass the expected deployment into the HTTP adapter and reject mismatched response provenance. One abort deadline covers HTTP headers and body consumption so stalled verification releases its operation-scoped observation ownership.
capabilities.limits: Automated browser coverage separates the local demo connector from controlled provider faults; manual injected-wallet behavior remains unverified.

capabilities.name: Digital-asset escrow
capabilities.behavior: Escrows ERC-721 assets, separates completion, pull claims, refunds, withdrawal, and token reclaim, and checks recorded liability against independently summed outstanding obligations. Each escrow sale reserves one buyer and rejects outsider funding on-chain.
capabilities.limits: Local test assets and test ETH only; contracts have not received an external security audit.

capabilities.name: EVM integration literacy
capabilities.behavior: Validates receipts, logs, block identity, deployment identity, ABI hashes, and runtime code on a local EVM.
capabilities.limits: Anvil behavior does not establish public-network finality or archive-RPC support.

capabilities.name: Event-driven backend
capabilities.behavior: Observes headers before requesting logs by exact block hash, orders events, applies pure projectors, and atomically advances source and checkpoint state. Verifies bound raw and decoded source evidence before rebuild and labels retained events with canonical and source-scan evidence. Resumed reindex operations reuse their verified captured target and durable catch-up checkpoint without repeating the source rewind. Source-refreshing reindex requires a verified backup, and an explicit source-incomplete rebuild transition records lineage before a full scan-start reindex. Classifies contradictory source content for verified archive and scan-start reacquisition while leaving pure missing rows on rewind/reinsert. Reconciliation refreshes the latest head after anchored comparison so publication freshness cannot reuse a stale pre-comparison sample. A checkpoint above the current indexing-depth eligible target fails closed until explicit reindex convergence. Live CURRENT requires convergence to the current depth-adjusted eligible target, not merely a fixed maintenance target. Persisted recovery-required evidence blocks ordinary writes; maintenance reindex releases it only after target proof. Public profiles project finalized blocks only and support a read-only secondary source audit.
capabilities.limits: Automatic recovery across arbitrary canonical branch changes remains outside scope; incomplete rebuild source requires explicit reindex. Public finalized-provider and archive behavior remains unverified; secondary endpoint configuration alone does not prove organizational independence.

capabilities.name: Database lifecycle
capabilities.behavior: Uses native Drizzle history, bundle-bound resumable migration markers, verified pre-migration backup proof, fresh-only environment ownership, managed environments, connection roles, signal-safe lock cleanup, incomplete-maintenance mutation gates, catalog seed, explicit deployed or predeployment backup identity, generation-safe restore recovery, and shared bootstrap/reset lifecycle ownership. Recovery completion acquires maintenance ownership and rereads the current operation marker before choosing or mutating recovery state. Marker updates use unique temporary files so unpublished crash residue cannot strand a matching resume. Backup records source readiness and projection evidence; maintenance archives are evidence-only and normal restore accepts only ready snapshots. Standard snapshots share bootstrap lifecycle ownership, restore owns it exclusively, and database-only restore rejects incomplete or changed bootstrap sidecars before quarantine. Reset persists intent before chain mutation and recovers only from explicit reset phase evidence. The database model classifies authority and recovery semantics for every migrated table, while documentation generation executes current migrations and rejects physical/model/reference drift. Standard deployed backups validate immutable bootstrap receipt schema and identity before publication and during verification.
capabilities.limits: A real process kill in the broadcast-to-hash persistence window and other listed database fault-injection cases remain incomplete.

capabilities.name: Cross-team interface contracts
capabilities.behavior: Publishes ABI, deployment, HTTP wire, database, and package export contracts for consumers. API CORS accepts one configured canonical frontend origin. Shared contracts include explicit Anvil, Ethereum, and Polygon profiles and the reserved-buyer field.
capabilities.limits: Generated artifacts require a current drift check after provider changes.

capabilities.name: Failure diagnosis and recovery
capabilities.behavior: Exposes projection status, action-wide receipt evidence, funding-specific projection proof, alternative-hash read-only recovery, per-event canonical source evidence, cross-tab journal serialization, anchored reconciliation, and operation-specific recovery commands. Seed persistence and reconciliation head failures preserve explicit recoverable or unverifiable evidence. Reconciliation preserves NFT collection identity, and source maintenance archives contradictory evidence before reacquisition. Transaction recovery rejects saved, configured, RPC-chain, or on-chain deployment identity mismatch before transaction lookup and preserves tab-local verification evidence when durable storage writes fail. Published maintenance markers remain authoritative across temporary-file crashes, and restore refuses archives captured during unfinished maintenance. Backup and restore preserve one bootstrap generation, while reconciliation distinguishes anchored comparison from publication-time head freshness. Local-only rebuild does not renew live RPC observation timestamps.
capabilities.limits: Hardware power loss, cross-device journal recovery, and some filesystem fault cases remain unverified.

capabilities.name: Release management
capabilities.behavior: Tracks generated artifacts, deployment manifests, schema contracts, and local readiness gates.
capabilities.limits: Local and remote gates are commit-specific; the verification record must name the exact source context and remote run instead of reusing an older source claim.

capabilities.name: Code review and delivery quality
capabilities.behavior: Provides local CI commands, resolved-target architecture fixtures, a PR template, and review responsibilities.
capabilities.limits: Repository artifacts describe a collaboration model; they do not prove a multi-person team used it or that remote settings are enabled.

capabilities.name: Roadmap and dependency management
capabilities.behavior: Maps P0–P5, D0–D5, DOC-P0–P5, blockers, and provider-consumer exit gates without inventing delivery metrics.
capabilities.limits: Planning artifacts are examples and current-state records, not historical sprint evidence.

capabilities.name: Onboarding and mentoring support
capabilities.behavior: Gives role-based entry paths, safe first changes, recipes, tests, and review checks.
capabilities.limits: These artifacts support onboarding; they do not prove mentoring sessions occurred.

capabilities.name: Remote cross-functional collaboration
capabilities.behavior: Defines async handoff, ownership, interface impact, blockers, and consumer acceptance gates.
capabilities.limits: No claim is made about an actual remote team, review event, or delivery history.
